title: Cross-lattice (D3Q15 vs D3Q19) acceptance of the conservative Allen-Cahn phase-field LBE
decision: Does one lattice-parametric CAC phase-field code path produce the SAME, analytically correct capillary physics on D3Q15 as on D3Q19 (the lattice the frozen verified D3Q19 module uses), within the owner 15% bound?
alternatives: A (chosen): keep the frozen D3Q19 CAC scheme (Liang et al. PRE 97 033309) and generalise only the velocity set + the two lattice-specific derivative stencils that lbmpy derives for D3Q15/D3Q19.
B: implement a separate D3Q15 code base (duplicate physics) -- rejected: no way to attribute a lattice difference to the lattice rather than to a code difference.
C: derive the D3Q15 Laplacian as the velocity-weighted 6*sum w_i (phi_i - phi) instead of lbmpy's 15-point stencil -- kept as a measured sensitivity arm, not as the default.

D: run lbmpy/walberla itself as the reference solver -- rejected for this round: need for a C/C++ code generation + compile toolchain on the nodes; lbmpy 2.0 source is read as the method/structure oracle instead (documented in oss_solutions).

E (adopted as the OSS-faithful configuration): mixed lattices -- phase field (h-population) on D3Q15 and hydrodynamics (g-population) on D3Q19, exactly as walberla's PhaseFieldAllenCahn app (oss_solutions row 363); implemented as lattice_phase/lattice_hydro in one code path.
hypothesis: H1: the analytic Young-Laplace law dp = 2 sigma/R and the model's own tanh interface solution are satisfied on both lattices with the same input sigma, so |sigma_rec/sigma_in - 1| <= 15% on each lattice and the two lattices agree with each other within 15%. H0 (rejected if any criterion fails): the D3Q15 velocity set cannot carry the CAC/HCH scheme at this resolution, e.g. it loses isotropy of the capillary force or becomes unstable.

outcome_metrics.sigma_rec: dp*R/2 from the static-droplet pressure readout (fp64 recompute), averaged over the final sampling window
outcome_metrics.cross_lattice_pct: |sigma_rec(D3Q15) - sigma_rec(D3Q19)| / mean * 100 at the same physical configuration
outcome_metrics.W_fit_pct: |W_fit - W_in| / W_in * 100 from the tanh fit of the radial/planar profile
outcome_metrics.profile_max_dev: max |phi_sim - phi_tanh(fitted)| on the interface band (dimensionless, 0..1 scale)
outcome_metrics.phi_drift_rel: |integral phi(t) - integral phi(0)| / integral phi(0) (conservative-AC invariant)

analytic_references: Young-Laplace, 3-D sphere: dp = 2 sigma/R (Young 1805; Laplace 1806) -- no fitted constant
CAC equilibrium profile phi = 0.5[1 - tanh(2 (y-y0)/W)] (Liang, Xu, Chen, Wang, Chai, Shi, PRE 97, 033309 (2018), Eq.(30)/(33); same profile family as lbmpy phasefield_allen_cahn)
discrete phase-inventory conservation (conservative AC): integral phi constant to round-off
prior in-repo verified point (not a free parameter, used only as a consistency check): benchmarks/verified/laplace_cac_phasefield sigma_rec errors <= 0.45% at 96^3/128^3, rho ratio 10/100, D3Q19
control_arms: CTRL_uniform15 / CTRL_uniform19: phi == 1 everywhere (single phase), so mu grad(phi) vanishes identically and the pressure field must stay uniform -> dp ~ 0. This isolates the pressure readout and the force chain from any real capillary signal.

stopping_rule: a Laplace arm stops when |dp(t) - dp(t-500)| / |dp(t-500)| < 1e-3 (evaluated every 500 steps after min_steps) or at max_steps; arms that hit max_steps are reported with converged=false and their dp kept (never silently discarded).

controlled: dx = dt = 1, cs^2 = 1/3, dtype float64, periodic box
nu = 0.1 in both phases (equal kinematic viscosity; mu = nu*rho per phase, harmonic mu(phi) mixing)
droplet initialised with the model's own tanh profile, p0 = 0.01
pressure readout bands: r/R in [0.95,1.05] (inside) and [1.6,2.2] (outside), both away from |phi-0.5|<0.45
changed: lattice: D3Q19 (19 velocities, face diagonals) vs D3Q15 (15 velocities, body diagonals)
grid/R: 48^3 / R=12 vs 64^3 / R=16 (resolution pair, same W and sigma)
lap_scheme: lbmpy 15-point stencil vs velocity-weighted stencil (D3Q15 discretisation sensitivity)
confounders: the D3Q15 Laplacian stencil has a different O(dx^2) error constant than the velocity-weighted one -- separated by the lap_scheme arm
spurious (parasitic) currents advect the interface and bias dp -- u_max reported per arm
the interface band r/R in [0.95,1.05] sits inside the drop only if R/W >= 3; true for every arm (R/W = 3.0 at R=12/W=4)
R = 12 with W = 4 is only 3 interface widths per radius; the 64^3/R=16 arm is the resolution control for that
an arm that does not reach its stopping criterion has a dp that still contains a transient -- flagged via converged

repetition_rationale: Deterministic float64 scheme, no random seeds: repetitions are the independent arms (2 lattices x the parameter sweep) plus one bitwise repeat of the primary D3Q15 arm (arm L15_n48_R12_repeat) to demonstrate determinism rather than assume it.
analysis_plan: sigma_rec from the final sampling window of each arm; error vs sigma_in
paired lattice comparison at identical physical parameters (same grid, R, rho ratio, W)
convergence flag + dp time series per arm reported, no arm discarded
failed criteria reported as failed (honest-FAIL), partial credit by criterion
